The Third and Fourth Derivatives of the Zero Wrappers' Expected Information

Source: R/d34e_zero_wrappers.R
zero_wrapper_d34expected.Rd

Compute the third or fourth derivative of the expected Hessian of zero_inflated() and zero_adjusted() families, on the parameter scale, by differentiating the expressions of zero_wrapper_dexpected() along each multiset of parameters. The parent enters through its expected Hessian and its derivatives up to the same order, and, for a discrete parent, through the log-mass at zero and its derivatives to order five.

Usage

zero_wrapper_d34expected(distrib, y, theta, order, threads = 1L)

Arguments

distrib

A family from zero_inflated() or zero_adjusted().

y

The response, read for its length.

theta

The parameters, the parent's followed by the mixing probability.

order

3L or 4L.

threads

The thread count passed to the parent's methods.

Value

A named list keyed as d3expected_names() or d4expected_names(), each component of length length(y), on the parameter scale.

Details

The entries are those of zero_wrapper_dexpected(). With \(f\) the parent's mass at zero, \(s_i\) its score there, \(E_{ij}\) the parent's expected Hessian, \(\zeta\) the probability and \(L = \zeta + (1-\zeta) f\), the zero-inflated entries are \((1-\zeta)E_{ij} + \zeta(1-\zeta) f s_i s_j / L\), \(-f s_i / L\) and \(-(1-f)^2/L - (1-f)/(1-\zeta)\), and the zero-adjusted discrete ones are \((1-\pi)[E_{ij}/q + f s_i s_j/q^2]\) with \(q = 1-f\). The derivative of \(f\) along a multiset of parameters is formed from the log-mass derivatives by \(\partial_{aR} f = \sum_{U \subseteq R} \partial_U f\, \partial_{a R\setminus U}\log f\), products by Leibniz's rule and reciprocals from \(A\,(1/A) = 1\), through the operations of zw34_memo(). The orders of the parent's expected Hessian derivatives are read from its own methods, closed form where the parent has them and the default stencil otherwise. The order-3 call reads the parent to order 3 and the order-4 call to order 4.

See also

zero_wrapper_dexpected(), distrib_d3expected_hessian()
